//: Typecheck config for the capture tool's DOMAIN UNIT TESTS (workstream A4).
SEPARATE FROM tsconfig.capture.json ON PURPOSE. The two have genuinely
different requirements, so folding them together would weaken both:
* tsconfig.capture.json typechecks the APP. It must resolve `gi://*` and
`ags/gtk4` through @girs/ and must therefore NOT see node:test.
* this file typechecks the TESTS. It needs @types/node for
`node:test`/`node:assert`, and `allowImportingTsExtensions` because the
test files import the domain modules with an explicit `.ts` suffix.
WHERE @types/node COMES FROM: `make capture-test` installs it into this
directory's own node_modules on demand (its capture-test-deps target),
exactly as it installs typescript at the repo root. `"types": ["node"]`
is a DECLARED dependency, not a request for something the machine happens to
have — without the install, this config cannot compile at all (TS2688).
The install MUST stay under tests/ and out of the app tree: this directory is
BELOW the app config's own directory, so the default typeRoots walk from
src/gui-tools/capture-tool/ upwards never reaches it. See tsconfig.capture.json.
tests/node_modules/ is gitignored; a committed node_modules is a deployment hazard.
Why the explicit `.ts` suffix at all: Node runs these files natively via
its built-in TypeScript type-stripping (node >= 22.6, unflagged from 22.18
for .ts). Node's ESM resolver does NOT do extensionless lookup, so
`import ... from "../../domain/settings"` would fail at RUNTIME. The
suffix is therefore load-bearing, not a style choice — and
allowImportingTsExtensions is what lets tsc agree with Node here.
`noEmit` is set, and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` is deliberately NOT
used: nothing here is ever emitted. These files are executed by Node, not
bundled by ags.
This config does NOT need the desktop stack: nothing under tests/ts/
imports `gi://*` or `ags/*`. See the capture-test target in the Makefile.
